disposition.reason: A neighbor appealed the Killington Planning Commission's conceptual master plan approval, with partial affirmative PUD findings, for a development of up to 328 residential dwelling units plus commercial space; this is a municipal appeal concerning permission for new housing.

evidence.quote: Appellant Stephen Durkee (“Appellant”) appeals to this Court a decision by the Town of Killington (“Town”) Planning Commission (“Commission”) granting
conceptual overview of the future development of up to 328 independently occupied residential dwelling units and 32,600 square feet of commercial and club facilities

project.description: Golf Course PUD: conceptual master plan for a residential and commercial development on about 229 acres in the Killington Basin Section of the Ski Village Zoning District, with up to 328 residential dwelling units and 32,600 square feet of commercial and club facilities

evidence.quote: suggested that the development would include up to 328 independently occupied residential dwelling units and 32,600 square feet of commercial and club facilities
for a proposed residential and commercial development on 229± acres in the Killington Basin Section of the Ski Village Zoning District of the Town

municipal_decision.description: Planning Commission Findings of Fact, Conclusions of Law and Order granting conceptual Master Plan Approval with partial affirmative findings under the PUD criteria of Regulations § 505

evidence.quote: “Commission grants conceptual Master Plan Approval, with partial affirmative findings under the PUD criteria set forth in [Regulations] Section 505 for the Golf Course PUD.”
The document is signed by five Commission members with signatures dated April 7, 2010.
Appellant represents that he owns three commercial and rental properties that are approximately a half- mile “as the crow flies” from the Golf Course PUD
Appellant is represented by Daniel C. Hershenson, Esq.

discretion.description: The appeal challenged the Commission's authority to grant conceptual master plan approval, the Regulations' compliance with the enabling statutes, and whether the proposal complies with the Regulations (findings on privacy, roadways and parking, water and sewer, natural features, landscaping and screening); the court decided only the authority questions, and the documents do not show whether the compliance contentions turned on evaluative standards.

observed_status.description: The court held the Commission had no authority to grant conceptual master plan approval, declared the Commission Order null and void, and dismissed the remainder of the appeal; no further proceedings are shown.

evidence.quote: Findings of Fact, Conclusions of Law and Order of April 7, 2010 is NULL and VOID and of no further force or effect.
This completes the current proceedings before this Court concerning the pending application.

judgments.note: Appeal of a Planning Commission decision (municipal) granting conceptual PUD master plan approval for up to 328 residential units; the approval did not itself authorize construction, but it is permission-stage review of new housing, so in scope.

The proposal is new residential and commercial development; the approval was conceptual with partial findings and no construction authorized, which is a weaker form of permission but still concerns new housing.
The application proposes 'up to 328' dwelling units, a ceiling in a conceptual plan rather than a firm count.
Conceptual master plan approval with partial affirmative findings; treated as approved since no conditions imposed on the project are described.
The court voided the only authorization (the conceptual approval); no remaining authorization exists in this docket, so denied, though the court did not deny the project on its merits.

Question 3 challenged compliance with PUD criteria (privacy, landscaping and screening, etc.), but the passages do not show an evaluative test was contested; the decided issues were purely legal authority questions.
The decision expressly calls it a de novo appeal, though it was resolved on summary judgment.
Filing date stated (May 10, 2010, deemed timely after furlough closure); the January 27, 2011 decision completed the proceedings; no Supreme Court appeal observed.

history.note: Neighbor appeal of Killington conceptual PUD master plan approval; order voided and appeal dismissed on summary judgment.
